Buyer Added Bid Specific SLA Text Clause(s) The following Instructions to Tenderers will apply for this purchase: - i. Raw Material: The raw material i.e. “999 Silver in the form of ingots” required for making Chhattars is t o be lifted by the vendor from India Govt. Mint, Hyderabad. ii. Packing: The individual silver chhattars shall be suitably packed to avoid damage of the chhattars and to retain the actual shape of the chhattars

iii. Custody and return of material loaned to contractor: Initially, the successful bidder has to submit material custody deposit in form of Bank Guarantee/Demand Draft/ NEFT from any Scheduled Commercial Banks as per the details given below. a) Material custody deposit equivalent to amount of 30 kg of pure silver (999 fineness) is to be submitted b y the successful bidder within 20 days from the date of issue of GeM contract and lift the pure silver (999) r aw materials of 30 kg from IGM Hyderabad within 10 days from the date of submission of material custody deposit. b) All other subsequent lots are to be lifted by the successful bidder within 15 days from date of intimation by IGM, Hyderabad. The Bank Guarantee will be valid till 60 days beyond the completion of delivery of finished products. The b ank guarantee is to be furnished in favour of India Government Mint, Hyderabad (A unit of SPMCIL). iv. Terms of Delivery: Overall contract period would be 1 year from the GeM contract date; and the staggered delivery to be mad e by the successful bidder firm as per following schedule. The bidder has to supply Four (4) nos. of samples each for 10g, 20g, 30g & 50g chhattars, within 20 days f rom the date of lifting of raw material. This sample chhattars will be tested at IGMH for checking the suitab ility as per specifications of the tender. After approval/acceptance of sample silver chatters and the staggered delivery to be made by the success ful bidder firm as per following schedule. Bidder has to supply first lot of finished silver chhattars within 30 days from date of intimation regarding a cceptance of sample silver chhattars by IGMH. For 2nd lot to 4th lot: Bidder has to lift the pure silver raw material from IGMH equivalent to denomination wise quantity of chhat tars mentioned in each lot after submission of equivalent Bank Guarantee against raw material, within 15 days from the date of intimation by IGMH and supply the finished silver chhattars to IGMH within 30 days fr om the date of lifting the raw material. v. Warranty: Warranty shall remain valid for a period of twelve months. vi. Terms and Mode of Payments: Payment will be made within 30 days on supply of full quantity of chatters as per delivery schedule mentio ned in the bid and on receipt & acceptance of goods by purchaser and on production of the following docu ments by supplier: i) Invoice indicating the total weight of goods along with the details mentioned in the bid document such as description, quantity, unit price, total value. ii) Packing list iii) Consignment Note iv) Delivery Challan along with e-way bill v) Test/Assay Certificates indicating physical dimensions and made composition for Quality Assurance vi) Manufacturers’ Guarantee certificate vii. Price Schedule: Price Schedule has been uploaded separately on GeM portal. The firm has to fill the Price Schedule as per IGMH format and same is to be uploaded in Financial Bid of GeM portal only. viii. Quality Control Requirements: (i) BIS hallmark (HUID) confirming minimum purity of 995 should be provided on individual finished Silver Chhattars (ii) The Silver chhattars need to have Test/ Assay Certificates indicating fineness (i.e., Metal compositions) and physical dimensions for Quality assurance as per technical specification. 9. Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) The Scope of the Work is detailed below: I. Scope of the Bidder: i. To carry out processes like rolling, blanking, annealing, washing, buffing/polishing, stamping/embossing / etching and Nakkashi/Meenakari work as per the design required by IGM, Hyderabad. ii. It is to be ensured that the finished silver chhattars should not have scratch marks/dents/defects on it a nd should be free from any surface defects, discoloration, cracks etc. iii. The firm is required to prepare & submit a sample for taking approval of the competent authority of IGM, Hyderabad before going for bulk manufacturing. iv. Purity is to be certified along with the Invoice & indicated on the silver chhattars. v. BIS Hallmark (HUID) confirming minimum purity of 995 should be provided on individual finished Silver chhattars. vi. The individual silver chhattars shall be suitably packed to avoid damage of the chhattars and to retain t

he actual shape of the chhattars. vii. To and fro transportation i.e. lifting of silver ingots from IGMH and delivery of finished chhattars to IGMH should be in the scope of bidder. viii. Weight of each silver chhattar should have positive tolerance; no negative tolerance will be accepted. ix. Process loss in manufacturing of silver chhattars, if any, to be considered in making charges of chhattar s itself. No additional process loss to be provided to the successful bidder. x. If the items delivered are rejected for any reasons, the firm has to lift & replace the same at their cost & risk. xi. The Picture, weight, quantity and dimensions of required chhattars are uploaded separately in Buyer Ad ded Bid Specific ATC document (Annexure-1) for reference. II. Scope of the IGMH: The raw material required for making total 6,000 pieces of silver chhattars (10g-3000nos, 20g-1500 no’s, 3 0g-1000 nos. & 50g-500 nos.) having minimum 995 purity (finished weight of 10g, 20g, 30g, & 50g) will be provided by IGM Hyderabad in the form of equivalent quantity of fine silver (999 purity) ingots and the sa me is to be lifted by the successful bidder. Quantity of silver raw material to be provided to the successful bidder by the IGMH as mentioned below. Sl. No. Item Nominal weight of e Quantity Weight of 995 Silver ach Chhattar 1. 10g Chhattar 10 g 3000 Nos. 30,000 g 2. 20g Chhattar 20 g 1500 Nos. 30,000 g 3. 30g Chhattar 30 g 1000 Nos. 30,000 g 4. 50g Chhattar 50 g 500 Nos. 25,000 g Total 1,15,000 g Considering positive tolerance of 2% in weight for individual items, total weight of 995 Silver will be = 1,15 ,000 g × 1.02 = 1,17,300 g, which is equivalent to 1,17,300 × (995/999) = 1,16,830.3 g of 999 Silver. Hence, IGM Hyderabad will provide 1,16,830.3 g of 999 Silver to the successful bidder III. Acceptance Criteria: i. Simple chhattar with dome and hook at the centre and nakkashi/meenakari work on the chhattar is as p er the requirement of IGMH. ii. Weights & Dimensions of the chhattars are as below; - Item Weight (+2%)(g) Diameter(mm) Height (mm) 10 g Chhattar 10 + 0.2 g 52 ± 10% 25 ± 10% 20 g Chhattar 20 + 0.4 g 75 ± 10% 30 ± 10% 30 g Chhattar 30 + 0.6 g 85 ± 10% 35 ± 10%

50 g Chhattar 50 + 1.0 g 120 ± 10% 50 ± 10% iii. Purity of silver chhattar should be minimum 99.5% (995 fineness). BIS Hallmarking confirming 995 finen ess should be provided on individual chhattars. iv. All to-and-fro transportation i.e. the receiving of the input material from India Government Mint, Hyderab ad ad & delivery of the finished goods i.e. chhattars at India Government Mint Hyderabad will be in the sco pe of the vendor. 10. Experience & Past Performance:-The Bidder should have experience of successfully manufactured and s upplied precious metal chhattars or items for the value at least Rs.41,00,000/- in any one of the last five y ears ending on 31.03.2026. 2. Capability-Equipment & manufacturing Facilities: - The Bidder must have the capability of manufacturing and supplying precious metal chhattars or items. 3. Financial Standing: i. The average annual financial turnover of the bidder during the last three years, ending on 31.03.2026 sh ould be at least Rs. 41, 00,000/- as per the annual report (audited balance sheet and profit & loss account) of the relevant period, duly authenticated by a Chartered Accountant. ii. The net worth of the Bidder should not be negative on 31.03.2026 and should not have eroded by more than 30% in the last three years, ending on 31.03.2026. Note for Bidders: a. For MSE & start up (registered for the tendered items) all experience and financial criteria shall be relaxed subject to having technical & quality capability & capacity. However, its capacity & capability may be verified (if necessary) by the IGM, Hyderabad. b. ‘Doctrine of Substantial Compliance’: The Pre-Qualification Bidding (PQB) and Prequalification Criteria (P QC) are for shortlisting of sources who are competent to perform this contract to ensure best value for mo ney from expenditure of Public Money. This process is neither intended to bestow any entitlement upon no r to create any rights or privileges for the Bidders, by way of overly hair-splitting or viciously legalistic inter pretations of these criteria, disregarding the very rationale of the PQB and PQC. Keeping this caveat in vie w, interpretation by Procuring Entity would be based on common usage of terminologies and phrases in pu blic procurement in accordance with the ‘Doctrine of Substantial Compliance’ and would be final. c. Along with all the necessary documents/ certificates required as per the tender conditions, the bidder sh ould furnish a brief write-up, backed with adequate data, explaining his available capacity (both technical and financial), for manufacture and supply of the required goods, within the specified time of completion, after meeting all their current commitments. d. Supporting documents submitted by the bidder must be certified as follows: All copy of supply/ work order; respective completion certificate and contact details of clients; documents issued by the relevant Industries Department; National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC); manufacturing licence, annual report, etc., in support of experience, past performance and capacity/ capability should be authenticated by the person authorised to sign the tender on behalf of the bidder. All financial standing data should be certified by certified accountants, for example, Chartered Accountant s II. Undertaking: - 1.
